<margin>This is the proof of the exhaustion of frugality.</margin>
<margin>To retreat is also to regret.</margin>
<margin>Calligraphic note: 〇</margin>
<margin>Not reaching.</margin>
<margin>Calligraphic note: 〇</margin>
<margin>Always like this.</margin>
<margin>Not because I consider it correct to act, but to wear it like one wears a reminder on the chest <note>original: "服膺"</note>.</margin>
<margin>And to contend with him again, then calamity will arrive.</margin>
<margin>Syntactic note: 〇</margin>
<margin>What I practice.</margin>
<margin>The appearance of leaning one's body to the side.</margin>

<term>Yin Wuyai</term> <gloss>a name, lit. Drinking-the-Boundless</gloss> Old Master remained indifferent and did not respond. Shicheng Qi returned the next day and said:

Discussion

"In the past, I had criticisms for you. Today, my heart has straightened out and settled. What is the reason?" The Old Master said: "As for those who are clever, wise, divine, or sage, I have already cast these aside. In the past, if you called me an ox, I accepted it as an ox. If you called me a horse, I accepted it as a horse. If one possesses the reality, and people give a name to it, if I do not accept it, I will invite calamity a second time. I submit, and I always submit. My submission is not because I believe that 'submission' has a form. Shicheng Qi, I carry this in my heart <note>referring to the previous margin note regarding "wearing on the chest"</note>, acting while avoiding my own shadow, treading..."

<summary>Shicheng Qi questions Laozi regarding his previous criticisms and his shifting attitude toward reputation and external labels, to which Laozi responds that he remains indifferent to titles and labels to avoid further trouble.</summary>
<keywords>Laozi, Shicheng Qi, reputation, labels, detachment, submission</keywords>
